title: Self-contained six-class secp256k1 rho with the exact 748-instruction step (126.3194)

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho algorithm specified in proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^126.3194 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). Subject to the explicit H1 heuristic and the failure estimates restated in proof.md sections 4 and 6, its recovery probability is greater than 0.39003 and therefore at least 0.39. Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes, preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units and charged in full, and nonuniform advice is zero. This is a deterministic-accounting revision of the public six-class construction in dddcbeb3-bc7b-4421-b946-70e15cb833d2 and bd8e6be5-913b-47a8-b097-526f4bf4be11, using the kappa=1.01 calibration and census of a6ae92da-3a0c-4493-84c1-bcfd6da47232 and the exact-table accounting of d14987fb. The proof restates the construction, merging lemma, failure bounds, doubling/traversal rates, field and batch-kernel derivation and the 114 explicit analytic rows, so it does not depend on unavailable supporting files. The ordinary step is charged at its exact 748 instructions: 634 counted AArch64 loop instructions (111 pass 1 + 523 pass 2) plus 114 analytic bookkeeping instructions. The public packages charged a conservative 129-row table (765 or 763 total); this package charges the 114 explicit sequences, with fallback, doubling, traversal and report paths priced separately. The counted 634 is derived in proof.md sections 5.1-5.2; the generated assembly is public and its hashes are in proof.md. It is a conditional analytic bound, not a new algorithm, practical key recovery, independently established production heuristic, or claim of official qualification. The declared Docker experiment was not run in this preparation because Docker is unavailable; the package's ledger path was checked locally.

experiments.purpose: Recompute the 114-row analytic step, the 748-instruction price, the 126.3194 work cap and the H1/Markov success floor with 80-digit Decimal arithmetic. It does not execute the counted AArch64 kernels; their self-contained derivation is in proof.md sections 5.1-5.2.
